body_text:
Cartesian product is associative only up to canonical bijection,
not literal equality under the ordered-pair encoding. The maps
$((a,b),c)\mapsto(a,(b,c))$ and its inverse identify
$(A\times B)\times C$ with $A\times(B\times C)$. This distinction
between equality and canonical isomorphism recurs throughout
algebra.
